title: Dungeon 23 (3.285...) and a look at The Dungeon Diary of Daedalus from Shieldice Studio
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aOOR5vp4Kl0

Daniel (@dungeondive) joins Dungeon23 — Sean McCoy's challenge to draw one dungeon room a day through 2023 — but on his own terms, and the reasoning is the most useful thing here. He doesn't like megadungeons, doesn't find them practical for his games, and knows he will never sustain a room a day. So he does a room a week and calls it Dungeon 3.285. Start small is the whole point.

The project is also a drawing practice, aimed at a book for Dungeon Dive patrons at year's end, with patrons supplying prompts along the way. His three January rooms establish the premise: on the planet Morago a burning disc fell from the sky into the Gandahar Mountains, and successive peoples have felt a diminishing urge to dig at the crater. The latest was a UFO cult whose name is written Qwolato but spoken only in breath. You enter by diving beneath a waterfall; the entrance hall holds a horned statue transfixed by three eternal braziers; a patron-prompted changing room stocks endlessly refreshed purple robes, with an initiation rite of washing over candles without spilling a drop.

Alongside it he surveys Shieldice Studio's The Dungeon Diary of Daedalus: room tiles, a five-room generator from dropped d6s, depth charts, dungeon uniqueness, light sources, a beast builder and traps.

----

Daniel scaled Dungeon23 down to a room a week rather than abandon it. Is a shrunken version of a community challenge still the challenge, or does the constraint do the work?
